summary: This bill requires the Secretary of Defense to add annual sports physicals, electrocardiograms, and specified blood tests (including metabolic panels, blood counts, and if needed thyroid and natriuretic peptide tests) to the periodic health assessments given to Armed Forces members starting in 2026.

scores.thoughts: The bill mandates additional annual tests (sports physicals, EKGs, blood panels, etc.) as part of military periodic health assessments. These new requirements will generate incremental costs for the Department of Defense's health program, thereby expanding government spending, albeit modestly and only within the military health system.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue measures.

The legislation expands required diagnostic services within the military health system (TRICARE/MHS). This increases the scope of publicly funded care delivered to service members, producing a modest shift toward more comprehensive public coverage in that specific domain.
No provisions address firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.
No provisions relate to immigration, visas, border security, or pathways to citizenship.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.
By requiring additional medical tests for all service members, the bill will increase defense health expenditures. This constitutes a direct, albeit small, increase in military spending.
No environmental, regulatory, or climate-related provisions appear in the bill.
The bill affects only active-duty military health assessments and does not alter civilian welfare programs such as SNAP, Medicaid, or housing assistance.
No education funding, school-choice, or federal education policy provisions are present.
No provisions concern drug scheduling, decriminalization, or enforcement.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No trade, tariff, or globalization measures are included.
The bill's added defense health costs contribute marginally to federal outlays and therefore to deficits, but the effect is too small and indirect to register beyond a negligible level.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related policies.
No foreign assistance or international aid provisions are present.
No voting access, election integrity, or campaign-related measures appear.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance provisions are included.
No labor, union, or workplace rights provisions are present.
No religious exemptions or anti-discrimination provisions are addressed.
